vocabulary.meaning: looking at a product in a physical shop but buying it online, often for a lower price
examples: Showrooming creates challenges for traditional retailers.
Customers may use a shop to test a product before ordering it online.

vocabulary.meaning: a business that sells products directly to consumers
examples: Retailers are adapting to online competition.
The retailer matches some online prices.

vocabulary.meaning: to check the costs of similar products before buying
examples: Smartphones make it easy to compare prices while shopping.
Many customers compare prices online before visiting a store.

vocabulary.meaning: relating to a physical shop rather than an online business
examples: Brick-and-mortar stores offer customers a chance to see products directly.
Some companies combine online sales with brick-and-mortar locations.
She examined the laptop in-store but made the purchase online.
Customers can complete a purchase through the app.

vocabulary.meaning: a reduction in the normal price
examples: The online shop offered a larger discount.
Discounts can strongly influence purchasing decisions.

vocabulary.meaning: the overall impression a customer gets from interactions with a business
examples: Good service can improve the customer experience.
Physical retailers compete through customer experience as well as price.

vocabulary.meaning: able or determined to compete successfully
examples: Stores need competitive prices.
Fast delivery can make an online retailer more competitive.

vocabulary.meaning: the quality of being easy and suitable to use
examples: Online shopping offers convenience, especially for repeat purchases.
Many consumers value convenience more than a small price difference.

vocabulary.meaning: a policy in which a retailer agrees to sell an item at a competitor's lower price
examples: The store offers a price-match guarantee.
Price matching may reduce showrooming.
